title: Clinical trial in people with celiac disease to analyze whether intestinal lactase activity is related to alterations in the intestinal barrier.
official: Clinical trial to evaluate the correlation between variation in intestinal lactase activity measured with LacTEST 0.45g and alteration of intestinal barrier integrity and/or intestinal permeability in patients with celiac disease
summary: Main objective: To determine whether LacTEST 0.45 g can be used as a marker of the histological integrity of the intestinal mucosa and alterations in intestinal permeability in pathologies involving damage to the intestinal mucosa, such as CD, and to monitor recovery.

interventions.name: LacTEST 0,45 g polvo para solución oral.

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
1. Adults aged between 18 and 70 years with suspected celiac disease due to compatible clinical symptoms and positive anti-TG antibodies and different HLA DQ2 and/or DQ8 haplotypes.
2. Ability to understand the nature of the study and sign the informed consent form.
Exclusion criteria:
1. Pregnancy or breastfeeding.
2. Liver cirrhosis or other chronic organic liver or digestive diseases, including digestive surgery, excluding appendectomy and cholecystectomy., since can affect permeability.
3. Moderate or severe renal failure since can affect permeability.
4. Total gastrectomy and/or vagotomy.
5. Portal hypertension (ascites, cirrhosis)
6. Taking immunosuppressants during the study since affect permeability.
7. Patients diagnosed with myxedema.
8. History of pentosuria and/or galactosemia.
9. Hypersensitivity to the active ingredient Gaxilose.
10. History of anticoagulant/antiplatelet treatment that cannot be withdrawn in the days prior to the endoscopy.
11. Known contraindication for endoscopy with multiple biopsies. Patients undergoing treatment with oral antiplatelet agents or anticoagulants who cannot discontinue such treatment 3-5 days prior to the intestinal biopsy.
12. History of neoplasia or active inflammatory, hemorrhagic, autoimmune, and infectious intestinal diseases. Any other untreated chronic disease that may cause diarrhea or malabsorption.
13. Severe and chronic mental illnesses, including psychosis.
14. Parkinson's disease, dementia, and other neurodegenerative diseases, since can affect permeability.
